target_process: Pre-eruptive edifice change from magma pressurization (eruption precursor)
region_site: Piton de la Fournaise, La Réunion
coda_window_s: n/r (slope of dtau vs tau; short scanning window)
stack_scheme: Daily stacks referenced to long-term stack
best_practice_note: First demonstration that ~0.05% pre-eruptive drops are continuously detectable from noise with weeks of lead time

target_process: dv/v tracking inflation (decrease), deflation (increase) and caldera collapse (strong drop)
region_site: Piton de la Fournaise, La Réunion
best_practice_note: Quasi-real-time CWI workflow distinguishing inflation, deflation, collapse phases

target_process: Pre/co-eruptive elastic (dv/v) and scattering (decoherence) changes; localization of changes
region_site: Piton de la Fournaise, La Réunion
stack_scheme: Daily stacks, referenced; coda at increasing lapse times
depth_sensitivity: Early coda = shallow (surface waves); late coda = deeper (body waves)
uncertainty_treatment: Weaver et al. coherence-based error formula
best_practice_note: Couples dv/v with waveform decoherence and lapse-time depth sensitivity to image/locate changes (shallow vs deep)

target_process: Inter-eruption magmatic/hydrologic velocity change
coda_window_s: windows after S arrival; >=5 with CCC>0.65
stack_scheme: Stack across several hundred repeating-earthquake families (multiplets)
dvv_amplitude: Generally <1% (≈2% spread over years if read as Vs change)
best_practice_note: Coda-wave interferometry on repeating-earthquake families builds a continuous single-station inter-eruption record

target_process: Velocity changes during 2004–2008 eruption; conduit/plumbing dynamics
coda_window_s: 15 s window starting 2 s after first motion
stack_scheme: Combines repeating-earthquake CWI with ambient-noise interferometry
best_practice_note: Cross-validates coda-wave and ambient-noise dv/v during an eruption

target_process: Pre-eruptive velocity decrease, corrected for rainfall/pore-pressure
region_site: Piton de la Fournaise, La Réunion
stack_scheme: Daily stacks vs reference; network-averaged dv/v
best_practice_note: Environmental (rainfall) correction is essential — hydrological dv/v is comparable to the pre-eruptive signal

target_process: Pre-eruptive velocity drop (intrusion/edifice damage) on sparse networks
region_site: Piton de la Fournaise, La Réunion (method also re Kawah Ijen)
best_practice_note: Single-station cross-component (SC) more stable than autocorrelation at low freq; one station 3.65 km from vent still detected the drop

target_process: dv/v tracking summit inflation/deflation (radial tilt); magma pressurization
coda_window_s: 30 s window, min lag = interstation dist / 0.8 km/s
stack_scheme: Daily NCFs stacked over 3-day moving window
dvv_amplitude: Order ~0.1%; long-term trend cross-correlation -0.73 with tilt
uncertainty_treatment: weighted dt-t regression; coherence>0.65, err<0.1 s thresholds
best_practice_note: ~231 pairs from 22 vertical-component summit stations; first robust multi-year dv/v–deformation correlation using lava-lake tremor as repeating source

target_process: Stress sensitivity of dv/v during volcano deformation (geodetic source); depth localization
depth_sensitivity: Changes concentrated in shallow structure (higher bands shallower)
best_practice_note: Multi-band analysis localizes velocity change to shallow structure and ties it to strain from a geodetic deformation source

target_process: Search for precursory velocity change before large dome collapse; sensitivity to tectonic quakes/environment
best_practice_note: Establishes ~0.05% detection floor via pair averaging; reports ABSENCE of precursor before July 2015 collapse (important null result)

target_process: Intense pressurization accompanying paroxysmal lava-fountain eruptions
components: Three-component autocorrelation (ZZ, EE, NN averaged per station)
depth_sensitivity: Near-field; varies with station proximity to vents
uncertainty_treatment: cross-coherence + squared misfit; reject dt err>0.1 s or coh<0.6
best_practice_note: Single-station autocorrelation captures pressurization at summit stations even on sparse networks

target_process: Crustal response to 2014 Bárðarbunga–Holuhraun dike intrusion (volumetric strain) + seasonal loading
depth_sensitivity: Multi-band probing across depths, including depths where geodesy is insensitive
best_practice_note: Demonstrates linear dv/v–volumetric-strain relation in compressional/dilatational dike regions; multi-frequency depth probing

target_process: Pre-eruptive velocity decrease (~10 days before onset); edifice damage/pressurization
coda_window_s: 30 s windows; start = dist/700 m/s + 30 s
best_practice_note: Separates stable microseism band (0.1–0.2 Hz) from volcanic-tremor band (0.3–1 Hz) to distinguish medium vs source-noise effects

target_process: Volcanic unrest / phreatic eruption; separating coseismic and seasonal medium changes
best_practice_note: Single-station measurements separate volcanic, coseismic, and seasonal contributions over a decade

target_process: Summit inflation (dv/v increase) then edifice damage + Upper East Rift Zone intrusion (decrease) before 2018 eruption
depth_sensitivity: Frequency-dependent depth discrimination across upper crust
best_practice_note: Three frequency bands separate response to earthquake shaking vs deep magmatic intrusion and discriminate depth

target_process: Velocity changes during 2018 caldera collapse; growth of caldera ring fault toward surface
stack_scheme: Coda Wave Interferometry with Repeating Earthquakes (CWIRE), per-cluster pairs
depth_sensitivity: Short-term changes distributed in depth; long-term changes concentrated near surface
best_practice_note: Repeating-earthquake CWI resolves depth partitioning of fast (deep) vs slow (shallow) velocity changes during collapse

target_process: Volcanic, tectonic and environmental (groundwater) influences on velocity over 22 yr
stack_scheme: Long-term NCF stacks; many dv/v series on a common grid
dvv_amplitude: dv/v increase during 2004–2008 crisis; seasonal cycles (% n/r)
best_practice_note: 22+ yr continuous ambient-wavefield monitoring; spatial imaging of many dv/v series separates volcanic/tectonic/hydrologic signals

target_process: Seasonal snow loading vs volcanic processes; eruption–seasonality link
coda_window_s: min lag 5 s, length 20 cycles (e.g. 5-25 at 1 Hz)
depth_sensitivity: Inversion places changes in upper ~300 m
uncertainty_treatment: slope SD from covariance; coherence weighting
best_practice_note: Cross-wavelet dv/v with depth inversion; seasonal snow signal must be removed before attributing changes to volcanic processes

target_process: Magma-reservoir inflation/deflation (400–500 day cycle); coseismic drops; areal-strain coupling
dvv_amplitude: ~1–2% (range -1% to +3%); rapid drops after large earthquakes incl. 2011 M9.1 Tohoku-oki
best_practice_note: 17-yr, 24-station record isolates ~400–500 day periodic dv/v tied to areal strain from magma inflation/deflation, separate from coseismic drops

target_process: coseismic velocity decrease and postseismic recovery from repeating earthquakes
region_site: 1989 Mw 6.9 Loma Prieta aftershock zone, California (also Parkfield repeaters)
stack_scheme: Repeating-earthquake doublets; delays vs pre-mainshock repeaters
depth_sensitivity: Shallow concentration inferred (coda delays exceed direct-wave delays)
dvv_amplitude: Direct-S delays up to ~6 ms, S-coda delays >15 ms after Loma Prieta; coseismic decrease then recovery
best_practice_note: Repeating earthquakes give a co-located repeatable source; larger coda than direct-wave delays diagnose shallow change location

target_process: dv/v sensitivity-kernel theory (travel-time change of multiply scattered waves)
depth_sensitivity: Spatial sensitivity kernel (incl. depth) from probability a wave traversed a location in a lapse-time window
best_practice_note: Foundational kernel for spatially localizing velocity changes from coda travel-time shifts under diffusion approximation; basis for later 3-D kernels

target_process: depth constraints on coseismic nonlinear strong-motion-induced velocity reduction
region_site: 2004 M6 Parkfield earthquake, San Andreas fault, California
stack_scheme: Repeating-earthquake travel-time delays before vs after mainshock
depth_sensitivity: Velocity change concentrates in top ~100 m (shallowmost crust)
dvv_amplitude: n/r (shallow S-wave traveltime delays; major shallow reduction)
best_practice_note: Shows coseismic velocity reductions are dominantly a shallow (top ~100 m) nonlinear site effect — key for separating fault-zone vs near-surface signal

target_process: coseismic velocity drop in a crustal-earthquake source region (fault-zone monitoring)
region_site: Mid-Niigata (Chuetsu) earthquake source region, Japan; F-Net station KZK (~24 km)
stack_scheme: Daily autocorrelations vs ~two-week pre-event reference; grid search (10000 trials, dv/v ±0.03)
depth_sensitivity: n/r (lapse-time dependence noted as future route to depth)
dvv_amplitude: -0.6% drop coinciding with the Mw 6.6 Mid-Niigata earthquake
best_practice_note: Single-station autocorrelation (passive image interferometry) avoids needing pairs; pick lapse window to exclude early scattered coda and stay above noise

authors_year: Brenguier, Campillo, Hadziioannou, Shapiro, Nadeau, Larose 2008
target_process: coseismic velocity reduction and postseismic relaxation (log(t) recovery) tracking afterslip on the San Andreas fault
region_site: Parkfield, San Andreas fault, California, USA
stack_scheme: 1550-day reference vs overlapping 5-day moving windows; 30-day time resolution
dvv_amplitude: ~ -0.1% coseismic drop after 2004 M6 Parkfield (also 2003 San Simeon), relaxing as log(t)
uncertainty_treatment: Averaged over 78 receiver pairs plus 5-day segments
best_practice_note: Multi-year continuous monitoring averaged over many pairs (78) enables ~0.1% detection and correlation with GPS afterslip/tremor

target_process: dv/v methodology (precision/stability of monitoring weak changes with noise correlation)
best_practice_note: Full Green-function reconstruction is NOT required for monitoring; only relative stability of the noise-source structure — validates passive dv/v against active measurements

target_process: coseismic damage and multi-year postseismic healing (shallow S-wave velocity drop)
region_site: Western-Tottori region, Japan; KiK-net borehole (surface + 100 m); 2000 Mw 6.6 mainshock
stack_scheme: Coda deconvolution of surface vs 100-m borehole records
depth_sensitivity: Shallow ground 0–11 m (between surface and 100 m sensor)
dvv_amplitude: ~30% decrease in S-wave velocity after mainshock, recovering over several years
best_practice_note: Randomly scattered S-coda deconvolution of surface-borehole pair robustly isolates the very shallow (<11 m) layer of largest coseismic drop

target_process: sudden coseismic mean shear-wave velocity drop in earthquake source region
region_site: 2004 Mw 6.6 Mid-Niigata earthquake source region, Japan; 6 Hi-net/F-Net stations <25 km
stack_scheme: Daily auto-/cross-correlations inverted daily for 2 months pre/post; pre-event reference
dvv_amplitude: Sudden drop of mean shear-wave velocity of a few tenths of a percent
best_practice_note: Coseismic drop confirmed with both AC and CC techniques across 6 stations, demonstrating robustness of passive interferometry

target_process: coseismic velocity change and its spatial distribution
region_site: Sichuan, China — 2008 Mw 7.9 Wenchuan earthquake fault zone
coda_window_s: ~25 s after ballistic, up to +-200 s lapse
stack_scheme: Noise cross-correlation stacking; sub-array comparison (156 broadband stations)
depth_sensitivity: Mapped via sub-arrays; dv/v consistent with volumetric strain, not sediment response
dvv_amplitude: Velocity drop up to ~0.08% in fault region post-earthquake; pre-event fluctuations within ~0.02%
best_practice_note: Compare across spatial sub-arrays to retrieve spatial pattern; relate to modeled volumetric strain to attribute change to in-situ strain not sediments

target_process: coseismic damage (near-surface weakening) and logarithmic healing
dvv_amplitude: ~10% reduction of shear-wave velocity in upper 100 m, then log healing
uncertainty_treatment: SD of travel times over events
best_practice_note: Deconvolution interferometry between borehole and surface sensors isolates the upgoing S wave; maps a ~1200 km wide weakening zone with log-in-time healing

authors_year: Rivet, Campillo, Shapiro, Cruz-Atienza, Radiguet, Cotte, Kostoglodov 2011
target_process: slow slip; nonlinear crustal deformation (strain-rate-dependent velocity change)
region_site: Guerrero, Mexico subduction zone (2006 M7.5 slow slip event)
depth_sensitivity: Surface waves sensitive to upper/middle crust ~5–20 km
dvv_amplitude: ~0.1% velocity decrease, far larger than volumetric strain (~1e-6)
uncertainty_treatment: previous-epoch referencing; no explicit error bars
best_practice_note: An aseismic SSE radiates no waves, so the velocity change cannot be a shaking/site response; time dependence tracks strain rate, evidencing crustal nonlinear elasticity

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and postseismic logarithmic healing
coda_window_s: ten periods, starting 7.5 periods after direct wave
stack_scheme: Daily cross-correlations vs long-term reference Green's function
depth_sensitivity: Upper several hundred m at two stations; ~km depth indicated at a third
dvv_amplitude: Coseismic drops stronger at higher frequencies, concentrated in southern fault zone
best_practice_note: 190 station pairs in three frequency bands isolate drop + log recovery while modeling seasonal variation; frequency-dependence constrains depth

target_process: coseismic velocity reduction and postseismic healing (mainshock + large aftershocks)
region_site: Southern Tohoku (Fukushima/Ibaraki), Japan; 58 Hi-net stations; 2011 Tohoku-Oki
dvv_amplitude: Up to ~1.5–2% nearest mainshock, with gradual healing; drops after 11 Mar and 11 Apr events
best_practice_note: Single-station vertical autocorrelation avoids needing pairs; spatial dv/v correlates with static strain (GPS) and peak ground velocity

target_process: depth-sensitivity methodology (coda-wave sensitivity vs depth)
components: P and S (Vp/Vs=√3); Rayleigh fundamental mode dominates shallow
stack_scheme: Averaged over 10 random medium realizations per configuration
depth_sensitivity: Surface waves dominate first ~6 transport mean free times; lapse time localizes dv/v in depth
best_practice_note: Normalize by transport mean free time; use lapse-time dependence of coda dv/v to discriminate shallow (surface-wave) vs deep (body-wave) change

authors_year: Brenguier, Campillo, Takeda, Aoki, Shapiro, Briand, Emoto, Miyake 2014
target_process: dynamic stress; coseismic velocity drop / stress sensitivity of pressurized volcanic fluids
region_site: Volcanic/geothermal regions of Honshu, Japan; 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-Oki
stack_scheme: Daily cross-correlations; linear inversion/regularization for continuous time series
depth_sensitivity: Relatively deep crustal volume (low-frequency 0.1–0.9 Hz Rayleigh waves)
dvv_amplitude: ~0.1% velocity decrease at volcanic regions after Tohoku-Oki
uncertainty_treatment: Stress sensitivity ~0.001 MPa^-1 inferred; detailed dv/v uncertainty n/r
best_practice_note: Low-frequency dense-network correlations map dynamic-stress-induced drops; concentration at volcanoes (not max shaking) reveals fluid-related stress sensitivity

target_process: coseismic velocity reduction + postseismic recovery / long-lived change
region_site: Epicentral region of 2008 Mw 7.9 Wenchuan earthquake, China
depth_sensitivity: Most prominent in 2–4 s band (~1–4 km), indicating depth-localized upper-crustal change
dvv_amplitude: Coseismic reduction up to ~0.2%; initial recovery then long-lived reduction
best_practice_note: Use multiple period bands of three-component correlations to separate depth-dependent dv/v; long-lived reduction interpreted as incomplete healing

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and recovery
region_site: South Napa, California (2014 Mw 6.0 South Napa earthquake)
depth_sensitivity: Likely within seismogenic depth (≤10 km); poorly constrained
best_practice_note: NCFs computed with MSNoise; band-pass 0.08–2.0 Hz then decimate to 20 Hz

authors_year: Gassenmeier, Sens-Schönfelder, Eulenfeld, Bartsch, Victor, Tilmann, Korn 2016
target_process: shaking-induced damage + postseismic healing (mesoscopic nonlinearity); thermal/environmental change
region_site: Station PATCX, Atacama Desert, Northern Chile (IPOC)
depth_sensitivity: Shallow: 90% of integrated sensitivity above ~114 m (6 Hz), ~168 m (4 Hz)
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal ~0.18%; transient coseismic drops ~0.49–0.62% for major earthquakes
best_practice_note: 8 yr of single-station autocorrelations isolate damage/healing via mesoscopic nonlinearity after removing thermal seasonal signal; log-time recovery

authors_year: Hillers, Campillo, Brenguier, Moreau, Agnew, Ben-Zion 2019
target_process: fault-zone monitoring; velocity changes interpreted as response to deep aseismic creep
region_site: San Jacinto fault zone, California (after 2010 M7.2 El Mayor-Cucapah, M5.4 Collins Valley)
stack_scheme: Average-waveform reference for stretching; MWCS also applied
depth_sensitivity: Top ~10 km (above proposed deep creep source below 10 km)
dvv_amplitude: n/r (two tens-of-days episodes of reduced velocity)
best_practice_note: Resolves two successive ~tens-of-days velocity-reduction episodes over a 200-day window around April 2010

authors_year: Wang, Campillo, Brenguier, Lecointre, Takeda, Hashima 2019
target_process: coseismic damage (short period) and postseismic/static-strain change (long period) across the crust
region_site: NE Honshu, Japan (2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-Oki earthquake)
depth_sensitivity: Entire crust; long-period (to 50 s) samples below ~5 km; coseismic amplitude decreases with depth
dvv_amplitude: n/r (short-period drops in strong-shaking region; long-period drops delayed up to ~6 months)
best_practice_note: Combine short-period sensors with tiltmeters as long-period seismometers to extend depth sensitivity through the full crust

authors_year: Mao, Mordret, Campillo, Fang, van der Hilst 2020
target_process: dv/v methodology (wavelet cross-spectrum travel-time change; frequency-dependent dv/v)
depth_sensitivity: Frequency-resolved dt(f,t) discriminates dv/v at different frequencies/depths; less spectral smearing than MWCS
uncertainty_treatment: wavelet cross-spectrum amplitude weighting; coherence threshold
best_practice_note: Wavelet cross-spectrum gives optimal time-frequency resolution, handles dispersion + cycle skipping (2-D unwrapping), recovers dt more stably than stretching/MWCS

target_process: coseismic velocity drop plus seasonal variation; crustal rheology
region_site: L'Aquila region, central Italy (2009 Mw 6.3 L'Aquila earthquake)
best_practice_note: 17-year single-station record separating coseismic from temperature-driven seasonal signals

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and postseismic recovery (months)
region_site: Ridgecrest fault zone, California (2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest earthquake)
stack_scheme: Daily autocorrelation functions vs mean waveform
depth_sensitivity: Shallow crust surrounding the fault zone
dvv_amplitude: n/r (short-term drop near rupture; none beyond ~50 km; max change scales with log distance and peak dynamic strain)
best_practice_note: Velocity drop confined within ~50 km of rupture; recovery 1–3 months depending on slip and triggered-slip context

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and rapid postseismic recovery in fault-zone material
stack_scheme: 10-min stacks; adaptive Gaussian smoothing (20 min growing to 24 hr over 3 days)
dvv_amplitude: ~2% regional average; up to ~8% near rupture-arrest and Coso geothermal region
uncertainty_treatment: Standard deviations tracked; stabilized via smoothing
best_practice_note: Exploit abundant aftershock waveforms (autocorrelations and P/S conversions) instead of ambient noise for high-time-resolution monitoring

authors_year: Sheng, Mordret, Sager, Brenguier, Boué, Rousset, Vernon, Higueret, Ben-Zion 2022
target_process: slow slip event detection; fault-zone monitoring
region_site: San Jacinto fault, Anza seismic gap, Southern California
depth_sensitivity: A few km depth; reduced near-surface sensitivity
dvv_amplitude: dV/V inferred from volumetric strain of a ~Mw 5.1 / ~0.2 m SSE (early 2014, ~2 months)
best_practice_note: Use repeatable train-generated tremors as a stable high-frequency source; dV/V derived via volumetric-strain simulations

authors_year: Mainsant, Larose, Brönnimann, Jongmans, Michoud, Jaboyedoff (2012)
target_process: Pre-failure velocity drop preceding catastrophic earthslide-earthflow; clay softening / pore-pressure rise
components: Vertical / surface-wave (Rayleigh) cross-correlation between sensor pairs
depth_sensitivity: Velocity change localized at base of sliding layer (shallow, a few m) from frequency-dependent analysis
dvv_amplitude: ~-7% surface-wave velocity drop over several days before the Aug 2010 failure (reported elsewhere as ~6% for the event)
best_practice_note: Foundational landslide dv/v study; demonstrated days-ahead precursor on a clayey landslide using short-distance sensor pairs and high-frequency surface waves

target_process: Water-table / seasonal hydrology monitoring in a deep-seated slow-moving clayey landslide
region_site: Avignonet / Mas d'Avignonet landslide, Trièves (French Alps), France
depth_sensitivity: Rayleigh sensitivity peaks ~2-3 m depth in 6-8 Hz band, tracking shallow water table
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal dv/v of order 1% (anti-correlated with water table)
best_practice_note: Shows dv/v tracks water table in deep-seated slow landslide; choose frequency band so Rayleigh depth sensitivity matches expected water-table depth

target_process: Shear-wave velocity structure / time-spatial Vs changes of flysch prone to mass movement
region_site: Just-Tęgoborze landslide, Carpathian flysch, southern Poland
stack_scheme: Cross-correlation / interferometric stacks; dispersion inversion (neighbourhood algorithm)
depth_sensitivity: Few m to tens of m (3-D Vs model of landslide body)
dvv_amplitude: n/r (focus on Vs structure / time-spatial Vs changes, not % dv/v)
best_practice_note: Shows high-frequency noise interferometry images Vs of flysch landslides; dense arrays + dispersion inversion give spatial structure

target_process: Earthflow dynamics from Rayleigh-wave velocity; velocity drop with acceleration and recovery with deceleration
freq_band_hz: n/a (active-source ReMi/MASW dispersion, not coda dv/v)
dvv_amplitude: Substantial Rayleigh-velocity drop on acceleration, slow recovery on deceleration
best_practice_note: Rayleigh-velocity changes track earthflow kinematics; combining passive interferometry with active MASW cross-validates

authors_year: Bièvre, Franz, Larose, Carrière, Jongmans, Jaboyedoff (2018)
target_process: Influence of environmental parameters (temperature, precipitation) on dv/v in a clayey mudflow; seasonal reversible variations vs precursor
components: Surface-wave cross-correlation; three pairs of sensors
freq_band_hz: ~5-15 (surface-wave band; reported sensitivity to shallow layer <=2 m)
depth_sensitivity: Shallow (~2 m or less); ~30-day lag between air temperature and dv/v
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal reversible dv/v smaller than the ~6% pre-failure drop of 2010
uncertainty_treatment: Correlation coefficient; seasonal-cycle modeling to separate from precursors
best_practice_note: Quantifies seasonal/thermal dv/v cycles that must be removed before precursor detection; ~30-day temperature lag locates sensitivity in the top ~2 m

authors_year: Colombero, Baillet, Comina, Jongmans, Larose, Valentin, Vinciguerra (2018)
target_process: Temperature-controlled long-term evolution of a prone-to-fall cliff; reversible vs irreversible dv/v and resonance
region_site: Madonna del Sasso cliff, NW Italian Alps (Orta Lake), Italy
depth_sensitivity: ~tens of m (temperature reference at ~20 m borehole)
dvv_amplitude: Annual dv/v +/-10% at 2-4 Hz; ~+/-5% at higher frequencies
uncertainty_treatment: Correlation coefficient (~0.9 at low freq) as reliability metric
best_practice_note: For rock cliffs, distinguish reversible thermal dv/v from irreversible precursors; track both dv/v and resonance frequency

target_process: Rainfall- and earthquake-driven dv/v; rigidity loss during M>=5 quakes and inhibited healing by rain/small quakes
region_site: Maca slow-moving Andean landslide, southern Peru (3-yr dataset)
components: Cross-correlation of station pairs; ambient noise plus local earthquakes
dvv_amplitude: dv/v drops below -1.2%; short-term -dv/v with 2-5 day lag after rain
best_practice_note: Demonstrates coupled rain+earthquake forcing; timing between forcings controls healing - monitor both triggers jointly

authors_year: Fiolleau, Jongmans, Bièvre, Chambon, Baillet, Vial (2020)
target_process: Pre-rupture monitoring of a clay-block failure; combined dv/v and resonance-frequency precursors
region_site: Harmalière landslide, French Western Alps (collapsed Nov 2016)
freq_band_hz: 1-12 (monitoring); dv/v in 2-4 and 8-10 bands; block resonance ~9-16
stack_scheme: Hourly records, daily averaging vs reference
dvv_amplitude: dv/v up to +/-10% at high frequency before rupture
uncertainty_treatment: Correlation-coefficient degradation tracked across bands; multi-parameter precursor timing
best_practice_note: Combine dv/v with resonance frequency; precursors appear at different times in different bands, so multi-band monitoring improves confidence

authors_year: Le Breton, Bontemps, Guillemot, Baillet, Larose (2021)
target_process: Review of ambient-noise dv/v for landslide monitoring; precursors, seasonal effects, spurious-fluctuation challenges
region_site: Global review (9 landslides monitored to date)
components: Cross-correlation of station pairs (and single-station variants discussed)
coda_window_s: end of direct waves to 5-10 periods (site-dependent)
depth_sensitivity: Shallow (meters to tens of m), set by high-frequency surface-wave sensitivity
dvv_amplitude: Pre-failure drops of several % on clayey landslides; seasonal cycles ~1%
uncertainty_treatment: Weaver et al. (2011) rms + SD over pairs/windows; discard CC<0.6
best_practice_note: Authoritative synthesis: confirms precursor ability on clayey landslides; stresses separating environmental/seasonal dv/v and checking for artifacts

target_process: In-situ rock-slope destabilization; near-real-time precursor dv/v drop minutes before slope failure
dvv_amplitude: ~-0.5% precursor dv/v drop ~40 min before destabilization
best_practice_note: Demonstrates short-timescale (minutes) precursor; needs high temporal resolution and instability checks for early warning

authors_year: Liu, Li, Liang, Zhang, Jiang, Huang (2025)
target_process: High-resolution 4-D imaging of rainfall infiltration via noise-based dv/v; diurnal and rain-driven changes
region_site: Xishan Village landslide, Sichuan Province, China
stack_scheme: 20-min interval CCFs vs reference (SNR>4 wave-packet selection)
depth_sensitivity: Rainfall infiltration to ~8 m resolved; 15 m (15 Hz) to 40 m (5 Hz)
best_practice_note: Dense array + multi-frequency dv/v yields 4-D depth-time infiltration imaging; high station count enables spatial resolution

target_process: Moisture-driven elastic changes in a slow-moving clay-rich landslide; seasonal soil-moisture control on dv/v / surface-wave velocity
region_site: Hollin Hill Landslide Observatory, North Yorkshire, UK (2-yr)
stack_scheme: Time-lapse interferometry + MASW between recording periods
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal velocity variation linked to soil moisture/saturation (qualitative)
best_practice_note: Dense 10-station array across hydrogeological zones; saturation controls elastic properties - couple with moisture/H-V data

target_process: Pre-failure dv/v on an open-pit mine slope; subsurface precursor ahead of surface deformation
depth_sensitivity: Subsurface slope (dense borehole geophone array beneath slope)
dvv_amplitude: Velocity decrease ~12 days before slope-failure initiation
uncertainty_treatment: Decorrelation/CC; comparison with radar surface deformation
best_practice_note: Borehole/buried arrays detect subsurface precursors before surface (radar) signs; promising for early warning in engineered slopes

target_process: Groundwater / water-table change driven by precipitation
best_practice_note: Founding 'passive image interferometry'; single-station autocorr + stretching with precipitation model

target_process: Theory: thermoelastic + poroelastic/hydrologic loading driving seasonal dv/v
region_site: Theoretical model, applied to southern California
depth_sensitivity: Analytic depth-dependent stress; near-surface (tens-hundreds m) with depth-dependent phase lag
dvv_amplitude: Predicts seasonal dv/v ~0.1% scale; hydrologic dominates thermoelastic in S. California
best_practice_note: Canonical physical framework to attribute seasonal dv/v to thermoelastic vs hydrologic strain

target_process: Precipitation-driven groundwater / pore-pressure change (fluid discharge)
region_site: TCDP borehole array, Chelungpu fault, Taiwan
best_practice_note: Fluid-discharge controls water-table equilibration and hence the dv/v timescale

target_process: Groundwater storage at mesoscale; thermoelastic + hydrologic modeling over 30 yr
region_site: Gräfenberg Array (GRA1-4), SE Germany (karst limestone aquifer)
uncertainty_treatment: LSQ slope error as inverse-variance weight; bootstrap
best_practice_note: Demonstrates decadal stability; thermoelastic and hydrologic contributions comparable when GWL changes small

target_process: Stress/pore-pressure (coseismic; precipitation tested, minor here)
components: Rayleigh surface waves; Vs change inferred
stack_scheme: Daily CCFs from 30-min segments; 1-yr reference, 30-day moving stack
best_practice_note: Distinguishes coseismic damage from hydrology; precipitation showed no clear dv/v effect here

authors_year: Wang, Brenguier, Campillo, Lecointre, Takeda & Aoki, 2017
target_process: Thermoelastic strain + hydrology (pore-pressure diffusion / precipitation)
stack_scheme: Daily CCFs; ~1-yr reference, moving-window current stack
depth_sensitivity: Uppermost crust (first few km); pore-pressure diffusion in Kyushu

target_process: Coda wave interferometry theory; velocity-change estimation from coda time shifts
dvv_amplitude: sensitivity grows with lapse time t (dt = -t·dv/v)

target_process: Ambient-noise preprocessing (normalization, whitening) for reliable correlations
best_practice_note: Canonical 4-phase preprocessing workflow: (1) single-station prep with time-domain normalization (one-bit or running-mean) + spectral whitening, (2) cross-correlation & stacking, (3) measurement, (4) SNR-based QC

target_process: dv/v error estimation / resolution & accuracy of MWCS
stack_scheme: current stack vs reference, weighted linear regression dt vs t
best_practice_note: Established MWCS error framework: dv/v from weighted linear fit of dt vs t with coherence weighting; measurement error scales inversely with SNR

target_process: Improving temporal resolution of dv/v monitoring (waveform clustering)
stack_scheme: waveform clustering to enhance daily stacks
best_practice_note: Waveform clustering of correlations (grouping by similar noise-source conditions) raises temporal resolution from ~30 days to 1 day while preserving dv/v accuracy

target_process: Precision/bias of the stretching method (dv/v error theory)
best_practice_note: Derived the precision of the stretching estimate: dv/v error depends on loss of coherence between reference and current correlations, the frequency bandwidth, and the coda time window

target_process: Spurious dv/v from temporal changes in ambient-noise frequency content
best_practice_note: Temporal variations in the ambient-noise frequency content produce SPURIOUS apparent dv/v; must verify noise-spectrum stationarity (or restrict to stable bands) before interpreting velocity changes

target_process: Software/workflow standardization (MSNoise) for dv/v monitoring
best_practice_note: Open, reproducible end-to-end Python workflow (DB-driven) standardizing preprocessing, CCF, reference-stack and MWCS dv/v with documented parameter choices

target_process: Phase-delay / dv/v estimation method comparison (DTW)

target_process: Denoising correlations (curvelet filtering) to improve dv/v temporal resolution
best_practice_note: Curvelet-transform denoising of daily correlations removes incoherent fluctuations while preserving coherent coda, enabling daily-resolution dv/v from short stacks
